terms.definition: Unpaid, part-time volunteers without legal qualifications who hear cases in the Magistrates' Court, usually sitting as a bench of three.
terms.examiner: Advised on law by a legal adviser (justices' clerk); say what they do in criminal and civil cases.

terms.definition: The qualities a candidate for the magistracy must show: good character, understanding and communication, social awareness, maturity and sound temperament, sound judgement, and commitment and reliability.
terms.examiner: A precise list earns the marks in a short-answer question on selection.

terms.definition: Twelve randomly selected members of the public who decide the facts and the verdict in Crown Court trials.
terms.examiner: Juries Act 1974 sets eligibility: aged 18 to 75, on the electoral register, resident in the UK for five years since age 13.

terms.definition: A verdict of at least 10–2 (or 10–1, 9–1) allowed after the jury has deliberated for at least two hours.
terms.examiner: Section 17 Juries Act 1974; useful in evaluation on the "rogue juror" problem.

terms.definition: A jury's ability to acquit against the evidence because it believes the law or prosecution is unjust.
terms.examiner: R v Ponting and R v Kronlid; a strong advantage point, and a criticism.

terms.definition: The rule that jury deliberations cannot be disclosed or investigated.
terms.examiner: R v Mirza; the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015 made disclosure an offence. Evaluate: protects jurors but hides misconduct.
